title: Xhaka gets a suspended fine for a fake Covid certificate, and the headline says "suspended for two years"
dek: A widely shared breaking post can be read as a ban from football. Court reports describe a fine he does not have to pay unless he offends again within two years.
what: Sky Sports News posted on Thursday 8 October that Granit Xhaka "has been fined £136,265, suspended for two years, for forging a COVID-19 certificate". Xhaka plays for Sunderland and captains Switzerland.

Reports by Dawn, Yahoo Sports and Newshub say Swiss prosecutors dealt with the case by summary judgment and gave him a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs, set as 50 daily rates of 3,000 francs. A suspended fine is not paid if the person commits no further offence during a probation period. Here the period is two years.

Xhaka admitted last month that he obtained a fake vaccination certificate in 2022, when Switzerland required one for some travel abroad. He said he acted out of mistrust of the vaccine and worry, and called it a mistake. The Swiss football association then left him out of its Nations League squad.
I could not find a report of any playing ban. I did not open the Swiss prosecutor's own order, so the figures rest on the news reports named below.
why: The post is short and has a siren in it. "Suspended for two years" can be read as a ban from football, so a fan who reads only the line comes away with a different case from one who reads the report.
next: The prosecutor's order and any club or federation statement would show whether anything beyond the fine applies.
